summary: Reviewed the table-booking slot-window changes, London date handling, submit idempotency, event redirects, and GSC redirect/robots fixes through failure-path and workflow integrity risks. The main risks are around async operations that can complete after the user has moved on, plus one boundary-time bug and one event redirect guard that appears to run too late. Overall the happy-path fixes are mostly sound, but a few unhappy-path workflows need tightening before relying on them in production.
appears_sound: Slot-window rendering is based on `availableSlots`, not raw `availability.time_slots`, before calling `pickSlotWindow` (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:646`).

Party-size threading uses the freshly clamped value through the availability request and closest-slot selection (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:954`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:901`).

Submit idempotency fingerprints meaningful booking fields and adds `_t`, `turnstile_token`, and `website` only after selecting the key (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1306`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:1426`).
Initial mount scroll is guarded by `wizardMountedRef`, so `scrollIntoView` only runs after later step transitions (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:601`).

findings.description: The new falsy-event redirect appears to run after canonical-segment handling, so the intended failure path may still crash or 500 if `anchorAPI.getEvent()` returns null instead of throwing. Failure sequence: API returns null, page computes or compares the canonical segment first, and the `/whats-on` redirect never executes.
findings.evidence: The diff shows `if (params.id !== canonicalSegment)` before the newly added `if (!event) permanentRedirect('/whats-on')` guard in `app/events/[id]/page.tsx:240`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: `getEventCanonicalSegment` or the surrounding code may tolerate a null event, but that is not shown in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Inspect the few lines above `app/events/[id]/page.tsx:240` or add a test where `anchorAPI.getEvent()` resolves null.

findings.description: Nearest-alternative loading has no cancellation or stale-search guard, so an older no-availability search can overwrite alternatives after a newer search has started. Failure sequence: user searches date/party A, quickly searches date/party B, A's alternatives resolve last, and the UI can offer stale alternative slots for the wrong search context.
findings.evidence: `runAvailabilitySearch` launches `void loadNearestAlternatives(input.targetDate, input.targetTime, input.targetPartySize)` without passing the active abort signal or a request token (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:941`).
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: If the UI only renders alternatives when the corresponding old availability is still active, the user impact is reduced, but that guard is not present in the shown code path.
findings.what_would_confirm: Add a delayed-response test with two consecutive no-slot searches and assert only the latest search can populate `alternativeSlots`.

findings.description: The default requested time wraps past midnight without advancing the default date. Failure sequence: a user opens the form late at night, `now + 1 hour` becomes `00:30`, the date remains today, and the search submits a time that already passed earlier that same London day.
findings.evidence: `getDefaultTimeValue` returns `toTimeString(next % 1440)` while `defaultDate` stays `today`, and `handleFindTable` only rejects past dates via `isPastLondonDate(date)` (`components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:156`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:537`, `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:962`).
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The management API may reject the stale date/time later, but the client still starts the user in a broken workflow state.
findings.what_would_confirm: Unit-test the form defaults at 23:15 Europe/London and assert the date advances when the default time wraps to the next day.

findings.description: The review-step Back action remains available during booking submission, and there is no visible stale-response guard for the in-flight confirm request. Failure sequence: user taps Confirm, goes Back before the API returns, changes slot/details, submits again with a new fingerprint/key, and can end up with the first booking completing after they thought they had left that flow.
findings.evidence: `handleConfirmBooking` starts an async submit and sets `loading`, but the review Back button is still rendered without a disabled/loading guard at `components/features/TableBooking/ManagementTableBookingForm.tsx:2217`.
findings.why_it_might_be_wrong: The `Button` component or omitted submit-handler code may globally block interaction during `loading`, but that behavior is not shown in the pack.
findings.what_would_confirm: Simulate Confirm then immediate Back/change/resubmit with a delayed POST and verify whether the stale first response can set `result` or create a second booking.

empty_categories: No raw-slot window regression found; the window is selected from filtered `availableSlots`.
No volatile-field idempotency regression found; `_t`, `turnstile_token`, and `website` are excluded from the fingerprint in the shown code.
No initial-mount scroll failure found; the mount guard prevents `scrollIntoView` from firing on first render.
No material failure-path issue found in the robots.txt `dpl` removal or the `/hr` redirect based on the pack.
